sense: the master’s son, as the slaves call him

evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 233: unde aurum efficiam amantī erīlī fīliō
Ter. And. 3.4.23: in nūptiās conjēcī erīlem fīlium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Erīlis, the master’s or the mistress’s, is the adjective of erus; poetic, and above all Plautine (Lewis & Short). The daughter is erīlis fīlia.

phrases.latin: unde aurum efficiam amantī erīlī fīliō
phrases.english: a way to get gold for the young master, who is in love
